title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 2 | Week 4 vs. New York Giants
headline: Little actionable news: LaFleur praised TE Elijah Higgins' blocking and development, said the offense is a pure progression system with no hard-wired target, and gave no injury updates on two sidelined players whose names are unclear in the captions.
summary: LaFleur said Arizona runs a pure progression offense, so the quarterback reads in order and isn't locked onto any one receiver, apart from some situational human element. He warned that the Giants' defense, led by a ball-hawking safety whose name is garbled in the captions, is stressing takeaways, including strip attempts on ball carriers. He talked about how teams train yards after the catch and said Arizona did well against the Chargers and only okay against Seattle. He was asked about two injured players, whose names the captions garble, and gave no timetable. He said he leaves it to the medical team and stressed return to play versus return to performance. He praised Elijah Higgins as a physical, smart tight end who is a load once he gets going, and said his best days are ahead of him. He also discussed how the team handles league officiating calls, how much he trusts analytics, and what separates great teams (sharp pre-snap execution). Weather at MetLife won't change the practice week.

signals.note: LaFleur praised Higgins' inline blocking and physicality, which supports a role as a trusted tight end, though he gave no snap or target commitments.
signals.quote: I think his best days are ahead of him.

topics.detail: LaFleur said the offense is a pure progression system. Whoever is first in the read is where the quarterback should look, regardless of the receiver, though a human element can matter situationally.

The Giants, especially a safety who plays the post well and comes down into the box, are aggressive about takeaways and punching the ball out. Arizona's players are aware of it and know all eleven defenders will go after the ball.

Asked about two players returning to the field (names unclear in the captions), LaFleur said both are doing well but gave no timeline. He is deferring to the medical team and said both want to return when they can perform at their capable level.
LaFleur called YAC a trained skill and said Arizona did a good job at it against the Chargers. Seattle closed space on them better and tackled well.

Rain at MetLife won't change practice. LaFleur said analytics are useful but he won't read much into them at this small sample size, and he wants the analytics team to show how opponents see Arizona's offense.

title: Jesse Minter Optimistic About Trey Hendrickson's Recovery Timeline
headline: Trey Hendrickson (finger) is out this week after a procedure the coach expects to be very short term. Ethan Burke may make his defensive debut, and Ronnie Stanley is being monitored after a good two days of practice.
summary: Minter opened by announcing that Hendrickson will miss this week's home game. The team got his finger fixed, and Minter thinks the absence will be very short term and best for the long run. He framed the absence as a chance for other pass rushers, with a few more snaps for existing players and possibly the first defensive snaps for Ethan Burke. Ronnie Stanley practiced Wednesday and Thursday, was not seen at the final practice, and the team will check how he feels over the next day. Carson Vinson got strong praise for his first start: no sacks allowed and a decent run game, even if it wasn't consistently effective. Andrew Vorhees is expected to get more of an opportunity, and Minter said he has had a really good camp. Minter said a player moving to center has handled the switch well and that the whole line should help him. Minter called the opposing interior lineman Jeffery Simmons a huge challenge and said the offense has a plan. Lamar Jackson has been getting his normal reps in practice.

title: Joe Brady Gives Injury Update For Game Vs The Patriots
headline: Bills list CB Christian Benford questionable after no practice this week, with Hairston and Igbinosun ready to step in. Keon Coleman is expected to play, T.J. Sanders is doubtful and Ray Davis is questionable.
summary: Brady gave the Friday injury report ahead of the Patriots game. A player the captions render as 'Keenan', most likely Keon Coleman, was limited but Brady said he'll be good to go. Christian Benford did not practice all week and is questionable, and Brady said the team will evaluate him through game day. Brady described the call to play as a joint decision among himself, the player and the medical staff, and said nobody will be put in a spot where they don't feel comfortable. T.J. Sanders is doubtful after his appendectomy, though Brady was pleased to see him practice. Ray Davis is questionable after being limited the last couple of days. If Benford can't go, Brady said Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun are getting the same reps and are ready to step up. He also praised Skyler Bell's preparation from last week's receiver injuries, the return value of Greg Dortch, and Dawson Knox's leadership and selflessness. He downplayed the Patriots rivalry, calling it just the next game on the schedule.

title: Dave Canales shares final updates before Sunday night against the Lions
headline: Jalen Coker is truly questionable and his call goes to game day, while Xavier Legette is out this week. Monroe Freeling is still in concussion protocol, and John Metchie III is ready to step in if Coker sits.
summary: Canales opened by praising a banged-up group that fought back from a daunting early-week injury list, and said some players still need to progress over the next day or so. Jalen Coker did a full individual period and some team work in the final practice, so he is limited. The team will move his work around again Saturday and wants to push the decision as far as possible, likely to game day. If Coker can't play, Ja'Seem Reed will be elevated, Brycen Tremayne, who made a couple of plays last week, is an option, and Metchie has practiced and taken reps. Monroe Freeling was cleared for full practice but still has steps to pass before he is cleared for contact, and Canales declined to detail the offensive line combinations if he can't go. Legette is out this week, which Canales said fits with the bye in Week 5, and he hopes to get him back quickly. In the secondary, the team is leaning on Robert Rochelle and Corey Thornton for depth and special teams, and Chau Smith-Wade is expected to step up. Canales also expects rain Sunday night to make the run game central for both teams, and he said the offensive line is showing good ownership in the run game.

title: Ben Johnson on QBs: 'We have guys we believe in' | Press Conference
headline: Caleb Williams is out this week, so Case Keenum or Tyson Bagent starts at QB vs. the Jets. Theo Benedet starts at LT again, and D'Andre Swift looks on track after a short-week injury report listing.
summary: Ben Johnson confirmed Caleb Williams will be out this week. He would not name the Sunday starter, saying the choice is between Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent, and the coaching staff is split on it. He said the 'hot hand' matters, but so does the body of work, and he trusts both quarterbacks. D'Andre Swift showed up on the injury report, which Johnson put down to a short week after Monday Night Football. He plans to work Swift out Friday and is optimistic about Sunday. Ozzy Trapilo is still being brought back and looked good in Wednesday's padded practice. He won't play this week, so Theo Benedet starts at left tackle. Johnson called Colston Loveland a trusted, versatile player and said he needs to get the pass catchers more involved. Loveland's receiving numbers have been limited by protection and blocking duties. He praised rookie safety Dillon Thieneman for his instant impact, with the defensive coordinator moving him around to put him near the ball. He also previewed the Jets' fast pass rush, led by David Bailey, and the matchup problems that tight end Sadiq and receiver Garrett Wilson pose.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: October 2nd, 2026
headline: Mason Graham (knee) has no update and may be getting an MRI, which leaves a major hole on the Browns' defensive line. Deshaun Watson is trending up with better protection, and Denzel Boston is emerging as a go-to receiver.
summary: Monken had no update on Mason Graham's knee injury and wasn't sure whether an MRI was scheduled, though he praised Graham's effort, intelligence and early production (four sacks in three games). Michael Hall returned after leaving the game with an ankle injury, and Adin Huntington played a lot of snaps in the interior. Monken said the defense was more aggressive and man-heavy under Rudy, a lesson learned from the Jacksonville loss. On offense, he credited better protection and a better run game for Deshaun Watson's improved rhythm and downfield aggression. He acknowledged Watson's two second-half giveaways and a late sack, but said ball security is improving and that Watson usually sees the field correctly. He called Denzel Boston tough, diligent and strong at the catch point, and said the offense tried to get him the ball early but misfired a couple of times. He also said the team has to clean up penalties (43 through four games), especially pre-snap ones, and praised the team's resiliency in a comeback win over Aaron Rodgers' team. Jared Verse's trash talk got praise because he backs it up with effort, and Carson Schwesinger was called a great player who doesn't say much.

title: Brian Schottenheimer on 105.3 The Fan | 10-02-26
headline: Joey Porter Jr. had a great first practice after the trade and Dallas hopes he can play Sunday vs. Houston, depending on soreness and communication with the safeties; Dallas will keep throwing fades to Pickens and Lamb, and Javonte Williams' strong run game is a plus.
summary: Schottenheimer spent much of the interview on the trade for Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr., describing him as tall, long, physical and a fit for any scheme because Dallas's zone calls carry match principles. Porter had a great first practice, and the team is hoping he plays Sunday, depending on how sore he is and how well he communicates with Caleb Downs and the other safeties. Schottenheimer said the move shows the team is in win-now mode, and he praised Dak Prescott as playing at an MVP level. He said Porter gives flexibility with Downs, but injuries in the secondary matter more to how Downs is used. Looking at Houston (0-3), he called it the most talented defense Dallas has faced, citing Will Anderson, Danielle Hunter, Stingley, Lassiter and Al-Shaair. He expects Nico Collins to be back and said the plan is to disrupt C.J. Stroud's timing. He owned the late-game mistake in Baltimore, saying his frustration and the mindset he put Dak in led to miscommunication, and that Dallas has revisited its protocols. He defended continuing to throw fades to George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb, and said Javonte Williams played terrific and the run game was very good, despite the red zone sequence that didn't finish the opening drive.

injuries.detail: Hopes he can play Sunday; will check how he moves and whether he is sore after a great first practice. Ability to communicate with the safeties will drive the decision.

title: HC Sean Payton on facing the 49ers: ‘It’s a well-coached team’
headline: Payton gave no injury or backfield news on his last practice day before facing the 49ers; the fantasy-relevant takeaways are a respect-heavy view of SF's defense (Fred Warner, red zone defense, a well-coached D-line) and praise for the offensive line.
summary: Payton spent most of this session on nostalgia and on the 49ers. He recalled the 2006 Saints' return to the Superdome and mentioned that Sunday's forecast is around 92 degrees, so the team has heat plans in place. He praised Quinn Meinerz for his athleticism, work ethic and toughness, and he said Mike McGlinchey and Ben Powers were key free-agent targets to rebuild the offensive line room. He said the line is the most important position group in the building. On San Francisco, he called Fred Warner a prototype linebacker and the bell cow of the defense whom Denver must plan around. He said the 49ers play good red zone defense and are a well-coached team under Raheem Morris-style defensive principles and Kyle Shanahan's balanced run and play-action offense. He suggested that some bad passes in the pocket can reflect a well-coached D-line. He also called D.J. Jones a respected leader and an important part of the team. No injuries, depth chart changes or skill-position usage were discussed.

signals.claim: McGlinchey is the starting right tackle and a reliable, consistent presence on the offensive line.
signals.note: A steady right tackle supports Bo Nix's pass protection and the run game against a strong 49ers front.
signals.quote: with Mike, you do know what you're going to get. And it's a good thing.

signals.note: Payton's strong praise of Meinerz shows how highly the coach rates the interior of the line, which helps Denver's rushing offense.

signals.claim: D.J. Jones is a respected leader and important to the defense, often facing double teams.
signals.note: He anchors Denver's run defense and faces his former team, which has McCaffrey in the backfield.
signals.quote: He's an important part of our fabric though I would say on this team.

topics.detail: Sunday's forecast is about 92 degrees, and Payton said the team will have plans in place for the heat.
Payton called Fred Warner the prototype linebacker and the bell cow of the defense. He said the 49ers play good red zone defense and present a lot of problems.
He praised Kyle Shanahan's balanced run game and play action, and he called the 49ers a well-coached team. He also said the defensive line is well coached.
He said the line is the most important position group in the building. He added that the McGlinchey and Powers signings were meant to remake the position room.
He reminisced about the 2006 Saints' Superdome return and an upcoming ESPN ManningCast appearance on Monday.

title: Campbell on SNF vs. Carolina Panthers
headline: Brian Branch is 'close' to returning to practice, while Jackson Meeks' role is mostly special teams for now and DJ Wonnum is beginning to produce opposite Hutchinson.
summary: Campbell said GM Brad Holmes was heavily involved in pursuing a trade (the Steelers deal was mentioned, and Dallas did what it wanted), and that the team is always looking to upgrade the roster, including the secondary, if the value is right. He framed Carolina as a dangerous, versatile offense with Bryce Young as the 'secret sauce,' with a run game built on keepers, boots and shots, and a trio of versatile tight ends led by Waller. Defensive keys are pushing the middle of the pocket with McNeill, Tyleik Williams and Skyler Gill-Howard, containing Young with Hutchinson and Wonnum, and not letting him escape or step up. He defended Jack Campbell, saying he is fine and is the team's 'bell cow' despite the linebacker calling himself out. He praised DJ Wonnum as a steady, consistent, lunch-pail edge who is starting to win one-on-one opposite Hutchinson, which should ease pressure on Hutchinson and the interior. Jackson Meeks is still raw at tight end and gets a few reps behind Sam LaPorta and Brock Wright, mainly contributing on special teams, and Jimmy Rolder may get some defensive snaps after a good special teams debut. Brian Branch is close to returning to the practice field and looks good.

title: Matt LaFleur pleased with the step Matthew Golden has taken in Year 2
headline: Matthew Golden is praised for his physicality and separation, while the Packers' offensive line is shuffled: Zeitler is working back in, Aaron Banks is still working through something, and 'Princeton' is out a significant time.
summary: LaFleur said the Packers have a plan for the offensive line but will finalize it after one more practice. He described a week in which basically three new bodies arrived, and he spoke positively about the veterans' impact, singling out Kevin Zeitler. Zeitler had no training camp or offseason, but he is feeling more comfortable each day and has a lot of reps from his long career. On Aaron Banks, who was doing rehab work on the side, LaFleur said only that he is working through it and the team will see where he is. A lineman referred to as 'Princeton' (not on the roster, so unidentified) suffered what looked like a non-contact injury and is expected to miss a significant amount of time. LaFleur said that was one of the team's deeper position rooms, but fewer bodies put more load on everyone else. He said the passing game needs more from the tight ends and backs, while the team also feels good about other receivers beyond Golden and Watson. He praised Golden for playing really good football, separating well, and improving the physicality that the coaches challenged him on a year ago. He also called Bengals linebacker Trotter a beast and a very physical, active young player. The forecast of roughly 90 degrees on Sunday was handled with hydration and nutrition.

title: Shane Steichen: Week 4 final update, Colts vs. Commanders

title: Liam Coen on Final Preparations for Bengals, Practicing the Right Way | Press Conference
headline: Liam Coen praised Brian Thomas Jr. after a quiet 23-snap, one-target game and said Bhayshul Tuten's efficient running is earning trust. Coen wants to get Tuten cleaner lanes for big plays.
summary: Coen said the Jaguars prepped well for Cincinnati after the win over New England, with a physical Thursday practice and a strong special teams period. He said Brian Thomas Jr. had a great week, connected with Trevor Lawrence on a number of passes Thursday, and that the team will need him and the other perimeter players to keep making plays. He praised the versatility and confidence of a young defensive back, apparently Jarrian Jones, who is still shaking off rust after an injury layoff and improving each week. A running back who appears to be Bhayshul Tuten was singled out for discipline, yards after contact and avoiding negative plays. Coen admitted the long runs haven't come yet and said the staff must give him cleaner runs through the first and second levels. He stressed that depth players need to be ready because anyone could be called on, and he mentioned talking with BJ Ojulari about that. He said road games make communication and shifts and motions harder, so the staff has to avoid overloading players. On Cincinnati, he praised Chase Brown as an underrated back, noted the Bengals' pass-catching talent, and said Burrow and Marvin Jones see every coverage. He also called Travis Hunter's ownership of a pass interference penalty a sign of real accountability.

headline: Justin Jefferson is officially out for Sunday vs. Miami (Dolphins), though KOC is targeting a return to practice next week; Jordan Addison is not mentioned, so expect Tai Felton, Myles Price and Jeshaun Jones to see bigger roles.

He believes Jefferson would have had a big game last week given how Minnesota was defended, but the offense adjusted and won anyway. Preparing without Jefferson has been good for the rest of the group, with young players like Tai Felton and Myles Price getting their first full game-plan reps in expanded roles, and Jeshaun Jones being asked to do more than his usual position. He praised Jeff Hafley and the Dolphins as a hard-playing, physical team, and Malik Willis as a dangerous passer and scrambler who will take deep shots and run quarterback draws. title: WATCH: McCarthy on the loss to the Browns
headline: McCarthy blamed pass-protection trouble against Cleveland's five-man pressures and situational mistakes for the 27-24 loss. The Joey trade the night before the game and Jamel Dean's in-game injury added to the secondary's thin depth.
summary: McCarthy said Cleveland brought aggressive five-man, man-to-man pressure from the start, which gave Pittsburgh protection problems all night. He said the offense needs to step out of tackles, separate, and give the quarterback time to work through progressions. He called the offense's early success and later stall 'the National Football League', but said the team made mistakes in all three phases and needs to be better on the road. His biggest disappointment was situational football, since the team puts a lot of time into it and came up short in the two-minute drill at the end. He admitted the defense missed tackles and praised Cleveland's balanced attack, saying the backs ran hard. On the trade, he said the front office had been working on it for some time, and he thought Joey could play at some point earlier in the week with a rep count in mind. He also said the timing, the night before the game, is part of the business. He acknowledged some heated sideline communication with Aaron Rodgers, saying he wished he hadn't used certain words. He said the secondary is hurt by Dean being in the game and that young corners will have to rally. He ended by explaining a pass interference call that was reversed after Jack Sawyer tipped the ball and didn't tell the sideline.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Kevin Winston (shoulder) is the only injury-report name and coach isn't overly worried. Carnell Tate and Anthony Hill drew praise, while Cedric Gray's role is shrinking in a crowded LB room.
summary: Saleh said everyone is expected to practice. Kevin Winston appeared on the injury report after falling on his shoulder, but Saleh is not overly concerned for the game and will check how he looks at practice. A couple of other players, including one he called 'Tajh', still have hurdles to clear but are trending the right direction. On the right guard situation, he said the staff is comfortable with its direction. He pointed to a sharp center on the interior and praised JC Latham as playing at a Pro Bowl level. He blamed the slow starts on poor execution in critical situations (third downs, drops, a mistimed throw, a special teams turnover, run defense) rather than on tempo or play-calling. He praised Carnell Tate's run blocking and route-running growth. At linebacker he said the room is deep (Cedric Gray, Anthony Hill, Cody Barton, James Williams). He acknowledged it's hard that Gray is playing less after starting last year, but said the staff will keep finding ways to get him on the field. He also praised Hill's length and range while saying he still needs to grow in running the defense's communication. For the upcoming game he said you can't simulate Lamar Jackson or Derrick Henry and the team will just play disciplined.
